playbook.beforeYouGo:
DESK LEAD — do not drive to Williamsburg for this one, and don't treat it like a door to knock on. Busch Gardens is worked from your desk: email and phone to the park's PR team. The working window is January, ahead of the spring previews — this lead sits quiet until then on purpose.

Why it's in your book: the park's visitors are our people. Most of Busch Gardens' crowd drives in from Hampton Roads — about an hour — and plenty come down from the Raleigh–Durham area for the weekend. Magpie's founding creators carry counted local audiences in exactly those drive markets, and this is the one lead in your book that speaks to both at once. Water Country USA is inside this same lead: one Communications team runs PR for both parks (their Media Room is a joint one), and Water Country is seasonal — May through September — so the spring conversation covers both parks at once.

Your route in: the PR team's published media inbox, bgwpr@buschgardens.com — that's the door their own Media Room gives out. If it sits silent, the press-release contact inbox is buschgardenswilliamsburg.pr@buschgardens.com, and the Communications line printed with both is (757) 253-3369. No named person is published — you're writing to a team, so write like it: short, local, specific.

introEmail.body:
Hi Busch Gardens Communications team,

I'm Tony Johnson — I live here in Hampton Roads, about an hour down the road, and I'm helping Magpie build its founding business list for our area.

Magpie is local influencer marketing. We're building a founding list of local creators — real neighbors here in Hampton Roads — and every creator on it is ranked by how many of their followers actually live here, counted from their own audience numbers. When we open, local businesses use those creators to get local people in the door, and every visit is counted.

Here's why I'm writing to you and not just the shops on my list. Your visitors don't live in Williamsburg — they drive in. Most of them come from right here in Hampton Roads, and plenty more come down from the Raleigh–Durham area for a weekend. Those are exactly the audiences our creators carry: Hampton Roads is our founding market, and we're building the Triangle roster alongside it. A creator whose followers are counted in your drive markets is worth more to the park than a bigger account three states away.

The way it would work is the way you already work with media: a hosted visit — a creator and a guest come experience the park (Water Country USA too, in season) and post about it — and the visit carries that creator's own code, so afterwards you don't get a guess about what it did. You get a count. You'd approve every creator before anything happened.

Busch Gardens is being invited to claim a founding spot now — first pick of creators when we open, founding pricing locked, and there's nothing to pay today. I'd rather show you than pitch you: could I get twenty minutes in January, when spring previews are being planned, to walk you through the counted local audiences for your drive markets? Or claim the spot here and I'll follow up: {claimUrl}

Thanks for your time,
Tony Johnson
Magpie — Hampton Roads
